title: Legacy role receipt producer/consumer boundary: fixed baseline regression evidence
author: pro_review

ownership.independent_scope: Read existing production and author new regression tests; not independent validation of an implemented fix.
ownership.scheduling: This is deferred C3b evidence, separate from the parent's next C3a benchmark slice.

conclusion.observed: A legacy role receipt produced successfully by persist_role_process_receipt is rejected by check_active_roles before legacy completion when the receipt exceeds the generic 65536-byte effect-file reader bound.
conclusion.concrete_public_case: 1200 simulated ordinary-width identity records produce a 67841-byte receipt. The writer returns True; the real SQLite trigger remains STARTED when public check_active_roles holds.
conclusion.not_observed: Neither large public case reached record_terminal or _remove_bound_receipt. No terminal-then-cleanup failure is claimed.

boundary_analysis.finding: The existing legacy writer emits schema, role/host, controller/root identities, nonce hash, descendant identities, updated_ns and optional seven-field trigger reference. No caller-origin or private payload body is emitted. It caps descendants at 4096 but does not enforce a receipt byte limit.
Serializes and atomically writes the entire supplied JSON with fsync; no byte cap.
The 1 MiB constant is an orphan-reader bound, not a producer admission limit. This orphan reader was not invoked by the new tests.
Even with no v2 owner, an existing legacy role-process.json is classified using the generic attempt-effect _read before returning the legacy route.
Rejects nonregular, multiply linked or >65536-byte files before parsing. The regular writer-produced large receipt hits its size limit.
Catches the classification HOLD and continues before polling/legacy settlement; active role and STARTED trigger remain.
Separate 256 KiB bound is visible in source, but not reached by these public tests because the earlier classification gate rejects both large cases.

fixture.real: Temporary IdeaLake/SQLite observe, lease, begin, started, receipt publication and check_active_roles/settlement.
fixture.simulated: Only Linux identity, process polling, descendant refresh, nonce enumeration and reaping seams supplied by the existing fixture; no actual descendants or signals.

cases.observed: Small receipt completes through the real public consumer; trigger TERMINAL, receipt/lock removed, OK result and empty active map.

cases.input: 4096 positive signed-64-bit start_ticks and seven-digit PIDs, within the writer count cap and _valid_identity contract.
cases.observed: Writer True and receipt >256 KiB but <1 MiB; public consumer holds and actual state is STARTED.
cases.limitation: Accepted metadata/API domain only, not a realistic host-uptime claim or 4096 actual processes. Original test name and later unreached assertion text are not evidence of an already-TERMINAL state.

cases.input: 1200 simulated seven-digit PIDs and ten-digit start_ticks.
cases.observed: Writer True, 64 KiB < receipt <256 KiB, pre-state STARTED. Public consumer returns HOLD path; expected TERMINAL assertion fails with actual STARTED.
cases.limitation: Actual publisher and SQLite consumer, simulated identity metadata; not a real 1200-process tree.

first_version.delta: Appended only the ordinary-width 1200-record public case; did not rewrite either original parameterized case or its assertions.

interpretation_and_limits: The two red cases expose one public legacy-classification size mismatch; they are not two independently proven cleanup failures.
No source fix, whole-suite run, legacy adoption, v2 role supervision proof, actual OS process-tree exercise, GPU work, provider request, host-wide scan or signal is claimed.
The existing fixture remains unchanged and its OS simulations are explicit; the tests do not weaken production to obtain their failure.

Earlier benchmark/tournament/debate/K=1 and prompt-budget 1 MiB versus manifest 256 KiB claims were not established and are not counted here. Prompt body aggregate and metadata manifest bounds are different objects.

Potential later C3b repair should align legacy receipt write admission and all legacy consumers without broadening the generic attempt-effect JSON bound or granting v2 owner authority from legacy metadata.
